previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, altered mental status, and hypoglycemia, found to have MRSA bacteremia from an infected left tunneled hemodialysis catheter. He presented in septic shock requiring pressor support and fluid resuscitation. The infected catheter was removed, and he was started on vancomycin after initial broad-spectrum antibiotics. A temporary femoral dialysis line was placed after a one-week dialysis holiday, followed by a new tunneled right subclavian catheter. His mental status improved, and surveillance cultures remained negative. He experienced a focal seizure due to underdosed Keppra, which was corrected. Knee pain was evaluated and managed as non-infectious effusion. He stabilized on vancomycin, with plans for a six-week course in extended care, and was discharged with updated medications and close monitoring instructions.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST, TWO VIEWS, ___.

HISTORY:  ___ male with hypotension.  Question pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral views of the chest are compared to previous exam
from ___.  Dual-lumen left subclavian line is in stable position.
The lungs are clear of consolidation.  Trace blunting of the left costophrenic
angle again seen.  There is no right-sided pleural effusion. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  Surgical clips project over the
thoracic inlet bilaterally.

Osseous structures again notable for bilateral, old posterior healed rib
fractures and mild wedging of mid thoracic vertebral bodies, unchanged since
___.  Degenerative changes again seen at the shoulders bilaterally
including calcification in the region of the right coracoclavicular region.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  Right knee pain.
COMPARISON:  Right knee radiograph on ___.  CT-Torso on ___.

Single AP view of the pelvis.  Additional view of the right hip and two views
of the right knee.

RIGHT HIP:  There is a deformity of the right acetabulum, suggesting an old
fracture.  Heterotopic ossification is seen in bilateral hips.  The SI joints
are not visible and probably fused.  There is compression deformity of the
right femoral head with joint space narrowing and subchondral sclerosis of the
acetabulum, not seen on prior CT-Torso on ___.  This finding is
suggestive of avascular necrosis.  

RIGHT KNEE:  Marked muscle wasting is seen in the right lower extremity with
marked demineralization.  The large spur on the inferior aspect of the patella
is unchanged from ___.  There is no acute fracture or dislocation in
the right knee.

Impression: Probable old fracture of the right acetabulum along with marked
muscle wasting (suggestng paraplegia). Probably fusion of the SI joints may
reflect spondyloarthropathy or relate to ? paraplegia. Probable AVN
rightfemoral head.

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease, seizure disorder, chronic right hip and
knee pain, recently treated for tunneled line infection, admitted to ___ for
symptomatic hypotension and hemodialysis, concern for septic hip on right.

TECHNIQUE:  Imaging performed at 1.5 Tesla using a body array coil.  Routine
protocol.

RIGHT HIP MRI WITHOUT CONTRAST:

The right hip is markedly abnormal.  The femoral head superior articular
surface is markedly irregular and there is an acetabular protrusio
configuration.  There is a small joint effusion, with slightly complex
content. There is extensive loss of hyaline cartilage. There is marrow edema
in the surrounding femoral head, extending to the femoral neck, and in the
surrounding acetabulum.  There is considerable edema in the muscles
surrounding the right hip joint, including the gluteus abductors, obturator
internus, and muscles about the proximal femur. Incidental note is made of
probable focal fat within the obturator internus muscle. There is probably
osteonecrosis in the right femoral head, which may account for the collapse of
the femoral head superior articular surface. 

The pelvic girdle is congruent.  There are mild degenerative changes at the
pubic symphysis.  

The left hip shows severe osteoarthritis, with marked cartilage thinning
superiorly and a subchondral cyst.  No gross joint effusion.  There is
horizontal linear low T1 signal associated with subtle edema along the
anteromedial femoral head inferiorly, suspicious for an atypical 
insufficiency fracture.  No evidence of osteonecrosis is seen in the left hip.

There is a small amount of free fluid in the abdomen.  Limited assessment of
pelvic soft tissue structures shows a small amount of free fluid in the pelvis
and probable small hydroceles.  At the periphery of these films, degenerative
changes in the lower lumbar spine are noted, not fully evaluated.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Limited study, partially degraded by motion.  

2.  Markedly abnormal right hip joint, with collapse and deformity of the
femoral head, and acetabular protrusio deformity. Suspect underlying femoral
head osteonecrosis.  Small joint effusion, with surrounding marrow edema and
with marked edema in the surrounding muscles.  The clinical significance of
these findings is uncertain.  There is evidence for a longstanding
abnormality, possibly osteonecrosis complicated by femoral head collapse,
which could result in a right hip joint effusion, marrow edema, and muscle
edema.  However, given the extent of the muscle edema, the possibility of
superimposed right hip joint infection cannot be excluded based on imaging.

3.  Severe osteoarthritis of the left hip.  

4.  Possible non-displaced insufficiency fracture in the left femoral head. 
This would require dedicated imaging for further characterization, though it
might be visible on radiographs. No evidence of left femoral head
osteonecrosis.

5.  Discogenic signal abnormalities in the lower lumbar spine, presumably
degenerative changes, but not fully evaluated on this scan.

Findings were discussed by phone with the covering in-house team by MSK fellow
Dr. ___ on the morning of ___.
